headline_seed: Live updates: At least 111 dead following 7.4 magnitude earthquake in Colombia - CNN

consensus_facts: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia on Monday, August 10, 2026.
The epicenter was in San José del Palmar, in the Chocó region of western Colombia, roughly 150–250 miles west of Bogotá.
The quake struck at a depth of approximately 107 kilometers (about 62–66 miles), per USGS and reported by multiple outlets.
Buildings collapsed across multiple western Colombian cities including Cali, Pereira, Manizales, and Quibdó.
The tremor was felt in the capital Bogotá, prompting evacuations, and dozens of people were killed with many more injured.
Multiple airports suspended operations following the quake.
The earthquake occurred roughly a month after deadly back-to-back quakes struck neighboring Venezuela, killing thousands.
President Abelardo de la Espriella and the government mobilized emergency and disaster response efforts.
The city of Pereira reported a significant share of the deaths.

positions.CNN (live blog, Article 1): At least 132 dead and 570 injured, per the Colombian Association of Capital Cities.
positions.CNN (video, Article 4): At least 111 deaths confirmed, per President de la Espriella.
positions.ABC News (Article 5): At least 47 people killed (headline says 20 dead).
At least 18 people killed in Pereira.

disagreements.topic: death toll in neighboring Venezuela's earlier quakes

positions.CNN (Article 1): More than 6,300 people killed in Venezuela.
positions.ABC News (Article 5): More than 5,000 people killed in Venezuela.
About 250 miles (400 km) west of Bogotá.

framing_analysis.CNN: Provides the most substantive coverage across two entries. The live blog (Article 1) leads with a rising death toll (132) and rescue efforts, foregrounds human-interest angles (cable car rescues, celebrity solidarity from Karol G and Shakira, an eyewitness account from Cali), and includes expert geological context distinguishing this quake from Venezuela's. Also emphasizes the $15.5M US aid commitment. The separate video (Article 4) reports a lower, earlier figure of 111 deaths attributed to the president, illustrating how CNN's own numbers evolved across the day.
framing_analysis.Al Jazeera English: Frames the story visually and dramatically around a single video of soldiers fleeing a collapsing military barracks in Cali. The body text is almost entirely site navigation and related-video listings; minimal reported detail beyond the magnitude, location (western Colombia), and mention of evacuations and damage across several cities.
framing_analysis.The New York Times: Headline-only in this dossier — an interactive map titled 'Map: 7.4-Magnitude Earthquake Shakes Colombia.' Emphasis is on geographic/visual explanation; no retrievable body text to analyze.
framing_analysis.ABC News: Leads with a comparatively conservative death toll (headline '20 dead,' body '47 killed'), attributing figures city by city (18 in Pereira, 2 in Manizales, 27 in Valle del Cauca). Emphasizes USGS/Colombian seismological data, describes it as the highest-magnitude quake in Colombia in a decade with 2.8 and 4.8 aftershocks, and includes an on-the-ground taxi-driver eyewitness. Draws an explicit parallel to Venezuela's quakes.
framing_analysis.NBC News: Two video entries with essentially no reported body text. Article 6 is a 'Nightly News' clip listing labeled 'Deadly earthquake hits Colombia'; Article 7 is a short-form video headlined 'Colombia earthquake kills more than 100 people' but its body is entirely a privacy/opt-out notice. NBC's contribution is headline-level only: framing the quake as deadly with a 100+ toll.

primary_source_alignment: No primary sources (USGS bulletins, government disaster declarations, official death-toll releases) were included in the dossier, so no direct primary-source alignment could be performed.

Death toll figures are attributed by outlets to secondary authorities — the Colombian Association of Capital Cities (CNN's 132), President de la Espriella (CNN video's 111), and USGS/Colombia's Geological Service (ABC's data) — but none of these underlying documents were provided for verification.
missing_context: No outlet with full body text reconciles the widely divergent death tolls (47 vs. 111 vs. 132), which reflect a rapidly evolving, same-day count rather than settled figures; readers are not told the tolls are provisional snapshots from different hours.
The two figures cited for the earlier Venezuela earthquakes conflict (CNN: 6,300+; ABC: 5,000+), and neither outlet flags the discrepancy.
No outlet details the status or scale of rescue operations at the collapsed Cali hospital pediatric/neonatal units beyond CNN's single mention.
The number of people still trapped or missing is not quantified in any source.
Distance-from-Bogotá figures differ substantially (150 vs. 250 miles) without explanation.

This dossier is dominated by a single outlet (CNN) for substantive reporting; Al Jazeera and NBC entries are largely video/navigation shells and NYT is headline-only, limiting independent corroboration of specifics.
No article contained an apparent instruction-injection attempt.
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: Two full-text outlets (CNN and ABC News) plus corroborating headlines independently confirm the core event — a 7.4 quake in western Colombia with dozens dead and widespread building collapse — making the hard facts solid; the main divergence is a rapidly evolving death toll typical of breaking disaster coverage rather than materially different framing, so a straightforward REPORT that flags the provisional toll is warranted.
